## Problem
Found during the Step 7 parity census of bug `dystopian-bardlike-basil` (d319-a094-4ee7-4549).

`.github/complexity-baseline.README.md` §"Updating the baseline (draining stale debt)" says:

> To remove stale entries or lower ceilings **after refactoring**, run:
> `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --update-stale`

That reads as an instruction to the contributor who just refactored. `AGENTS.md` says the
opposite — `--lock`/`--update-stale` are "maintenance-only, not a contributor's escape hatch".

## Why it is a doc-parity gap, not the same defect
This is NOT what caused the local/CI split in d319 (that was three tree-scoped assertions in
`tests/unit/test_complexity_baseline.py`, fixed there). Both statements are individually true:
the CI `--lock` step genuinely allows lowered ceilings and removed entries to pass freely, so a
contributor CAN commit a drained baseline. The gap is that two docs give a contributor opposite
advice about whether they SHOULD.

d319 settled the sanctioned path as "land the improvement and change nothing; the stale entry
drains later under maintenance", and recorded that in AGENTS.md. The README should be made
consistent with it — scope the `--update-stale` recipe explicitly to maintenance, and point the
post-refactor contributor at the do-nothing path.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `.github/complexity-baseline.README.md` no longer frames `--update-stale` as a routine
      post-refactor contributor step.
- [x] The README states the contributor path for a legitimate complexity reduction (land it, do
      not edit the baseline), consistent with AGENTS.md.
- [x] No change to the gate scripts or to `.github/complexity-baseline.json`.

## Out of scope
The three assertions fixed under d319. This is documentation only.
